title: Customize the player UI
lead: Reference for UI ownership, custom components and cleanup. Start with the implementation guide for standard UI, CSS and layout examples; use this page when extending them.

blocks.text: Compare the screen and its code

The construction code shows the selected theme’s component layout and links to its source. Its comments stay in English. Theme switching retains the player and source while replacing the app-managed UI.

PlayerConfig.ui enables SDK-managed UI. The SDK loads the configured UI assets before calling style.uiManagerFactory; use the SDK editor to inspect that callback. Choosing an app theme switches back to the app-managed UI. Keep only one owner of the UIManager to avoid duplicate controls and event handlers.
Choose a starting point

rows: Use standard controls
Use Default (Bitmovin) in the app. For an independent app needing the SDK's complete responsive variant selection, use UIFactory.buildUI from bitmovin-player-ui.
Change colors or sizes
Add a class to the standard tree and style it with CSS or SCSS. Neon is one example.
Add components or change layout
Recompose the component arrays in UIContainer and ControlBar.
Display custom information or actions
Extend Label, Button or ToggleButton. Scores and live wall-clock labels are examples.

blocks.text: UIManager connects the player and UI. UIContainer is the root of the displayed components; ControlBar holds playback controls; Container arranges components. Spacer expands the gap between them. Keeping these roles separate helps distinguish appearance changes from playback-engine configuration.

blocks.text: The app's DefaultUIFactory wraps the standard desktop/main component tree to expose autohide. It does not reproduce all small-screen, TV, advertising and empty-state variants supplied by UIFactory.buildUI. CSS themes use the same wrapper. Compare them as this app's desktop UI examples.
Choose UIConfig and UI ownership

rows: UI language, visible settings and component defaults
UIConfig.localization, componentLayoutOverrides and componentConfigOverrides
Apply in UI settings or the SDK editor. The app-managed mode rebuilds the UI; the SDK-managed mode recreates the Player.
Colors, dimensions and spacing
Skin CSS loaded after the base CSS
Compare Default and Neon and inspect the target classes. A UIConfig change does not rewrite CSS rules.
Components, order and custom behavior
UIContainer / ControlBar components and custom Button / Label classes
Edit a factory such as Compact or Premiere and rebuild. GUI theme selection chooses an existing composition; it is not a free-form component-layout editor.
Media, audio and network behavior
PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and PlayerAPI
Follow the PlayerConfig / SourceConfig chapter. Adding a UI button cannot create a track absent from the stream.

blocks.text: For an app-managed UI, set PlayerConfig.ui to false and own the UIManager lifetime. The implementation guide shows a complete standard-UI setup with UIConfig and its stylesheet.

items.label: Standard UI setup and supported component overrides

blocks.text: Use componentLayoutOverrides for new layout overrides rather than the older playbackSpeedSelectionEnabled option. Overrides accept the component types supported by the SDK, not arbitrary custom class names.

For SDK-managed UI, apply an empty object to PlayerConfig.ui in the SDK editor. This app uses the distribution at location.ui / ui_css and passes settings through style.uiManagerFactory. The SDK owns that manager’s release. Selecting an original theme returns to app-managed UI; do not attach a second manager over the existing one.

blocks.text: Create and release a UI

This TypeScript example runs inside the repository workspace, where @showcase/ui-shared and its compiled CSS are available. Pass the player element and your Player license to createPlayerWithUi, then load your SourceConfig with the returned player.load(). Calling usePremiere replaces only the UI, and release removes the UI before destroying the player. The flag shown matches the GUI experiment above; setting it to true restores the speed selector.
Change appearance with CSS
Neon adds a skin class to the Default component layout. Load override CSS after the base stylesheet and scope it to the skin so that other themes are unaffected.

items.label: Neon factory and scoped CSS examples

blocks.text: Change the component layout

The components array determines control order. The Compact example in the implementation guide shows how to move PlaybackTimeLabel relative to SeekBar. Rebuild the code to change placement; the GUI selects existing layouts.

Create fresh components for each UIManager and release the previous manager before attaching them. The Compact example omits the central play overlay, volume, settings and subtitle overlay; add those components when needed.
Reuse the result in your application

items: Choose whether you need only CSS, a different component tree or a new component. Keep player loading and playback configuration separate from UI construction.
For a project in this workspace, import the required factory and @showcase/ui-shared/css. @showcase/ui-shared is a private workspace package, not a package published for npm installation.

For an independent project, install bitmovin-player and bitmovin-player-ui with the versions used by this repository as a reference. Import bitmovin-player-ui/dist/css/bitmovinplayer-ui.css, then copy or adapt the required factory, custom components and skin rules with their license notices. App-specific names such as PremiereUIFactory are defined in this repository, not in the SDK.

Transfer the applied UIConfig values and the separate factory options such as hideDelay. If the theme needs recommendations, markers or playlist callbacks, supply those from your own application; the construction example does not export that app data.
Compare playback, keyboard focus, fullscreen, source changes and repeated UI replacement. Restore the previous UI or release the UI and destroy the player when leaving the screen.

blocks.text: Selecting a theme in the app retains UIConfig overrides. When testing a modification, restore each changed setting or reload the app before comparing. Browser-stored playback preferences and resume positions may remain. The UI settings chapter explains which media and components each setting needs.
Topics in the detailed guide
The in-app customization guide provides a component catalog, UI variants and TV navigation, gestures, styling and event handling. Use it when extending a component beyond the examples here.
Common UI modifications

items: Add or remove a control by editing the ControlBar component array.
Keep controls visible by setting UIContainer hideDelay to -1.
Recolor one element by checking its target class and CSS specificity.
Show title and description with TitleBar and SourceConfig values.
Show the next videos using RecommendationOverlay and metadata.recommendations.
Create a label that follows a player value by extending Label and updating it from events.

blocks.text: Hide custom labels

Label.hide() adds the bmpui-hidden class. In UI 4.23.0, the standard label's hidden style is scoped to its ui-label class. Setting cssClass replaces that base class, so a custom label needs a matching hidden style. Use cssClasses to add styling classes while retaining the base class, or include an explicit rule when replacing it. The shared stylesheet includes this rule for WallClockLabel and BehindLiveLabel.

Test the transition from live to on-demand playback after the clock has displayed text. A label that is empty on a fresh on-demand source can have zero height even when its hidden style is missing. Check retained clock text, the hidden class, actual CSS display and showing the label again. This stylesheet is used by the Web app, custom UIs on iOS and Android, and both React Native hosts. tvOS uses native System UI and Vega uses Kepler controls.
Release custom components

Call super.configure from configure and subscribe to playback events to update the display. Release timers, event subscriptions and auxiliary components from their owning component release method. Removing a UI from the screen alone does not establish that its resources have been released, particularly with repeated theme changes.

The shared UI package also includes cleanup fixes for auxiliary objects in the pinned UI library. When adapting a component, keep its release handling with its event subscriptions and timers; otherwise theme replacement can leave work running after the UI has disappeared.

Guide examples such as UIVariant, TV SpatialNavigation and VR do not mean that every corresponding control is implemented in the current Web app. Distinguish GUI controls, examples requiring code changes and capabilities requiring physical devices.
Replace UI during SDK events

The player can already be delivering an event when its listener is removed. For example, replacing the UI from a SourceLoaded, SourceUnloaded or Playing handler can leave another handler from the previous UI in the current delivery. Removing subscriptions prevents future events but cannot undo work already in progress.

The bundled Player UI patch marks a UIManager as released before cleanup and ignores later variant resolution and deferred configuration callbacks. This prevents the retired controls from being attached over the replacement UI. Release your own components once, remove their subscriptions and timers, and check that their owner is still active before deferred work changes the screen.
UI customization FAQ

rows: Controls overlap or a click is handled twice

Check whether SDK-managed UI and an app-created UIManager are both active. For app management, set ui: false and release the previous manager before rebuilding. Remove custom component subscriptions when their owner is released.
There is no setting to move a component
UIConfig changes supported behavior and overrides. Layout is defined by the UIContainer / ControlBar components arrays. Follow the Compact example, edit the factory and rebuild.
The UI setting changes but its control is missing

Some compositions, including Compact, omit a settings menu or subtitle overlay. Compare using a theme that contains the needed component. External-display components also depend on browser and device support.
The title or description ignores UIConfig

A nonempty SourceConfig.title / description takes precedence over UIConfig.metadata. Use SourceConfig for content-specific text. To test UI metadata alone, load the source after setting its corresponding field to an empty string.
A custom label stays visible after hide

Replacing the base class with cssClass can bypass the standard hidden rule. Follow the custom-label explanation above: retain the base class or add CSS for the custom class together with bmpui-hidden.
A previous setting remains after switching themes
Theme selection preserves UIConfig overrides. Restore changed values for a comparison. Browser-stored resume positions are separate state; check setting restoration and stored data separately.
